reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Draft (the paragraph's first eight sentences): "Decide to do it. How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? etc. Preview what you are going to do. Will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end?" It appears once in CONTEXT.txt at the head of its paragraph, with the recording line and the stop lines following it, so it does what the_change says: Emulate's version of those sentences with the old "this" kept in the second. Against SOURCE.txt it differs from the words it replaces in three small ways: "Deciding to do it." became "Decide to do it." (the imperative of his published "Decide what kind of encouragement is welcome"), "Something else?" became "etc." (still an open slot after spacious and warm and held), and the colon after "Preview what you are going to do" became a full stop. Every item of the meaning to keep is still there in the same order: what kind of encouragement (spacious, warm and held), then previewing eye closure ("Will you close your eyes?"), any repeated exit and re-entry ("Will you come out and go back in again?") and the return ("What will you do at the end?"). His third kind, "a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling", is not named, but it was not named in the words replaced either. I found no claim, fact or first-person statement added. In context the section runs think, safe place, decide, plan, so "Decide to do it." follows the safety paragraph as the next step. Its "it" is the practice that the two paragraphs before call "this" ("spend on this", "safe place to do this", "Don't do this if"), and the next sentence restates it as "do this", so the pronoun points where it should ("Decide to do this." would remove even a moment's doubt after the safety paragraph's last clause about deepening, but I don't count that as needed). "Make it spacious? Make it warm and held?" takes "it" as the way you coax yourself, as the replaced words did. Tell rows: T02 is PRESENT. The draft is eight short prompts in a row, each doing one job and handing to the next, which is the compressed-listicle cadence, and the writer's ledger line that it is "not part of a run of compressed commands" is not right for this card. I judge it justified here: the paragraph's job is to get the reader to make three separate pre-session choices, which reads as a checklist in a "Before you begin" section; the same steps in the same order are in his published guide and in the paragraph being replaced; the change adds no step and removes none; and the paragraph goes on to reasons and a counter-case ("You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do."). T09 and T13, which the D9 finding asks about, I checked at passage level: the section notices things outside this paragraph (the "whatever." aside, "A no will stay a no.", "no change is not a positive change") and its sentence weights vary, so I count them as covered by the T02 justification and not as separate findings. I also looked at T07 ("etc." reads as a real open-list marker, the same job as "whatever." earlier in the section), T12 (the list is open, not a closed pair), T19 ("Preview what you are going to do." is an instruction with content, and the colon that made it a list announcer is gone), T24 (the text answers none of its questions), T06 ("warm and held" is the article's own vocabulary), T15 (no rarer words swapped in, and "this" is put back), T26 (the "Make" openers are parallel list items) and C01 to C04; none is happening. Linter findings, each judged: "B7 short landing at paragraph end" is a false hit from reading the draft alone, since "What will you do at the end?" is the eighth sentence of a paragraph that goes on; accepted. "D9 follows the source order" is true by design (same passage reworded, same order) and nothing is reordered or cut; accepted. "E23 paragraph of instructions" is the T02 point above; accepted for the same reasons. "E36/E41 heavy second person" (12.2 per 100): the guide speaks to the reader as you and the replaced words had the same count; accepted. "O29 a run of three or more questions": the three are the reader's own pre-session choices from his published preview, the text answers none of them (so not a self-answered question), and a person planning a session would ask each; accepted. "R1 action it near a paragraph start": answered by context as above (the section's subject, two paragraphs of "this", restated as "this" in the next sentence, and the words replaced opened the same way); accepted.
